characters.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Runaway Room
characters.name: Susato Mikotoba
characters.description1: A judicial assistant sent to Britain on a study tour. She's the epitome of a refined Japanese lady and a huge help to me always.

characters.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Runaway Room
characters.name: Mael Stronghart
characters.description1: The Lord Chief Justice, who wields absolute authority in judicial matters, including the appointment of lawyers. He's a thoroughly intimidating man.

characters.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Runaway Room
characters.name: Magnus McGilded
characters.description1: The defendant in this case. He's an incredibly wealthy philanthropist with a wonderful reputation in London. I'm to defend him as a test of my worthiness to become a lawyer.

characters.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Runaway Room
characters.name: Barok van Zieks
characters.description1: A prosecutor known as the Reaper of the Bailey. Supposedly, the souls of those he prosecutes are eternally damned, one way or another.

characters.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Runaway Room
characters.name: 'Thrice-Fired' Mason
characters.description1: The victim. A skilled but poor brickmaker who apparently owed the defendant a considerable sum of money.

characters.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Runaway Room
characters.name: Beppo
characters.description1: The driver of the omnibus on which the murder took place. He's an eyewitness to the incident.

characters.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Runaway Room
characters.name: Bruce Fairplay
characters.description1: A gentleman who works as a city banker. He witnessed the incident from his seat on the roof deck of the omnibus.

characters.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Runaway Room
characters.name: Lay D. Furst
characters.description1: An apprentice milliner who witnessed the incident from his seat on the roof deck of the omnibus.

characters.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Runaway Room
characters.name: Gina Lestrade
characters.description1: A young woman who witnessed the incident from her hiding place aboard the omnibus on the night of the murder. She was discovered by the defendant.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Runaway Room
evidences.name: Armband
evidences.description1: An armband I inherited from Kazuma. It identifies the wearer as a defence lawyer throughout the Empire of Japan.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Runaway Room
evidences.name: Autopsy Report
evidences.description1: A report prepared by the Scotland Yard coroner. It gives the cause of death as internal haemorrhaging as a result of a single stab wound to the abdomen.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Runaway Room
evidences.name: Crime Scene Photograph
evidences.description1: A photograph of the victim taken on the omnibus. The knife in his abdomen is clearly visible, but his face is partly obscured from view by an old, crooked hat.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Runaway Room
evidences.name: Defendant's Leather Gloves
evidences.description1: The leather gloves the defendant was wearing at the time of the incident. There is a bloodstain on the right glove.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Runaway Room
evidences.name: Omnibus
evidences.description1: The eight-seater omnibus that was the scene of the crime. There were passengers both inside the carriage and on the roof deck that night.
evidences.description2: The scene of the crime. There is a bloodstain visible on the frame of the skylight when it's open.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Runaway Room
evidences.name: Murder Weapon
evidences.description1: A largish knife that was found lodged in the victim's abdomen. Its quality and fancy ornamentation suggest it must be quite valuable.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Runaway Room
evidences.name: Debtors' Ledger
evidences.description1: A catalogue of people who had borrowed money from the defendant at a high rate of interest. It includes the victim, who owed twenty guineas.
evidences.description2: Among the defendant's list of debtors is Bruce Fairplay, who would have been due to repay his loan imminently.

testimonies.testimony: There was blood on both hands of the assailant. I sincerely and distinctly remember that!
However...I, I suppose you might say that I didn't see the exact moment the stabbing transpired...if that matters.
I remember seeing the knife. And, and I remember seeing both of the attacker's hands with blood on them.
I, I d-didn't actually s-see anything myself. No. N-Not until I h-heard that scream.
Anyway, the fact remains! There can't have been anyone else inside that carriage, or we all would have seen!

turns.summarizedContext: The witness Beppo, Fairplay, and Furst are testifying about the crucial moment the crime was perpetrated.
reasoning: Fact 1: The witness claims nobody is in the carriage, or they would have seen
Fact 2: The evidence suggests there is a storage space under the omnibus seat that the witnesses could not see.
Prop 1: If there is a place that could hide a person, then the person from the top of the omnibus could overlook the possibility that this person is the actual culprit.
